questions.q: What is the main challenge in keeping a lava moat glowing?
a: Replacing the heat that the air constantly draws away
Finding enough rocks to fill the trench
Keeping the smoke from entering the house
Stopping the lava from melting the driveway
questions.why: Lesson one says air cools the lava, so insulated coils must pump back the roughly 100 kilowatts it loses.

questions.q: About how much does the electricity for a one-meter lava moat cost per day?
a: $600 a day
$6,000 a day
questions.why: Using ten cents per kilowatt hour, Munroe estimates sixty thousand dollars daily for a moat one meter wide and deep.

questions.q: At a constant 1g acceleration, how long would the trip to the moon take?
a: About four hours
About twelve hours
About three days
About ten minutes
questions.why: Lesson two says accelerating at 1g, the same pull we feel from gravity, gets you to the moon in around four hours.

questions.q: What does strontium-90 in someone's teeth suggest, according to Munroe?
a: They were a young child during above-ground nuclear tests
They grew up drinking leaded gasoline fumes
They were vaccinated against smallpox as a child
They spent their childhood near a coal plant
questions.why: Lesson three says strontium-90 entered children's teeth during nuclear testing from 1945 to 1962, marking many Baby Boomers.

questions.q: What larger point does the book make about absurd scientific thinking?
a: Weird ideas and abstract thinking can lead to real innovation
Only practical problems deserve serious research
Science is too dangerous for everyday use
Common sense beats careful calculation
questions.why: The overview argues that strange ideas gave us the airplane, computer, internet and smartphone, so abstract thinking has value.
